records.region: Central California, upper San Benito River–Hernandez Reservoir–lower San Benito River–lower Pajaro River coastal corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Completed bounded representative Pajaro River system identity for the selected San Benito headward corridor, Hernandez Reservoir passage, lower San Benito River and downstream Pajaro River to the coastal terminal. San Benito River and Hernandez Reservoir retain their distinct names; the representative identity is not a scalar label for every selected reach.
records.completion_scope: All twenty-three parts of the sole selected mainstem fragment were considered against four overlapping readable original USGS map views. The chosen opening, upper river bends, Hernandez Reservoir inflow/passage/outlet, middle and lower San Benito corridor, actual San Benito–Pajaro confluence, lower Pajaro River and actual coastal endpoint setting have ordinary-scale source correspondence. Connected original cartographic features establish the through-links; nearby labels or model connectivity alone are not substituted as proof. Beach-breach status and exact contemporary mouth/bank position are outside this bounded result, not missing inter-waterbody transfers.
records.supported_name_scope: San Benito River for the selected upper and middle river reaches; Hernandez Reservoir for the impounded passage; Pajaro River for the receiving river below the actual confluence and its coastal terminal setting.

scope_limits: Formal registry status, official name-transition vertices, naming history and Korean forms are unverified.
Pajaro River is a representative receiving-system identity; the selected San Benito River reaches and Hernandez Reservoir are not renamed.
The chosen eastern opening is not an official or ultimate source claim, and the modeled length is not an official river length.
Mapped channel symbols and wetland/impoundment features establish geographic corridors, not perennial flow, current water extent or operating state.

The actual endpoint is in the Pajaro coastal outlet setting. The short generalized terminal line cuts a local bend and shore; the original does not establish a current open breach through the beach or an exact contemporary mouth.

records.region: New Hampshire–Maine, Rocky Branch–Saco River–Camp Ellis coastal corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Completed bounded representative Saco River system identity for the selected small-feeder–Rocky Branch–Saco River–coastal corridor. Rocky Branch and the initial unnamed feeder remain distinct upper components; adjacent ponds, old river courses and widened managed reaches retain their own scope. This representative identity is not a scalar name for every selected reach.
records.completion_scope: Four successful and visually inspected original USGSTopo corridor views, fifteen original-pixel reading crops/details and private orientation aids cover both selected mainstem fragments, the chosen small-feeder opening, Rocky Branch/Saco junction, all intermediate selected corridors, the Fryeburg pond-channel setting, Hiram and Union Falls widenings and outlets, meaningful tributary junctions and actual coastal terminal. Map-depicted water connections, not model connectivity or nearby labels alone, establish the ordinary correspondence. Initial and terminal model shapes are expressly generalized; exact vertex/bank agreement and current operations are not required or asserted.
records.supported_name_scope: Rocky Branch for the mapped mountain valley and lower Jericho reach; Saco River for the trunk below their Glen-area junction through the downstream corridor, lower estuary and mouth. The small opening feeder remains unnamed.

scope_limits: The short mountain-side opening feeder is unnamed in this finding. The nearby Lower Stairs Brook label is not extended to it, and the modeled initial northeast kink is not asserted to follow an exact mapped channel. The source nevertheless depicts its local drainage into Rocky Branch.
The representative Saco River identity does not rename Rocky Branch, the initial feeder, Old Course Saco River, tributaries or the adjacent named ponds.

The rendered final extension crosses part of the Camp Ellis shore/spit before ending in open coastal water. The mapped river mouth just south of that extension connects the same estuary and receiving water; an exact all-water terminal trace is not claimed.
Service refresh metadata do not prove a current field survey, water level, flow direction at every side channel, dam operation or navigation route.
Formal registry status, formal name boundaries, Korean name and an accepted product name remain unverified or unset.

records.material_pending_reason: The western mainstem opening into the Turbio corridor and the extreme tributary feeder south of Lago Guillelmo remain unestablished in the inspected originals. Other receiving river, lake and terminal components are supported; the two headward gaps form one material-pending status.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Puelo is directly established for the receiving trunk, and Turbio, Manso and distinct lake components are identified. Whole selected representative identity remains uncompleted because two actual headward links are unresolved.
records.completion_scope: Puelo is directly supported as the receiving river, with distinct Turbio, Manso and lake components. All five selected fragments were inspected, but the western mainstem opening and the extreme feeder south of Guillelmo remain geographically unestablished. The system stays source-material pending; no scalar, Korean or automatic name is assigned.
records.supported_name_scope: Puelo is directly established for the receiving trunk, and Turbio, Manso and distinct lake components are identified. Whole selected representative identity remains uncompleted because two actual headward links are unresolved.

scope_limits: Actual natural-watercourse correspondence of both chosen headward openings remains unresolved; missing depiction does not establish absence of a river.
No uniform scalar name spans the Turbio, Puelo, Manso and lake components.

Constituent historical IGN sheet dates, current national-registry status and Korean forms unverified.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
